messages:
Ava Dunn: heads-up — starting a short thread to align on Q4 prioritization for routing policy work. we have multiple customer asks (isolation lanes, tenant anti-affinity, cross-region failover) + product wants clearer launch criteria. can we checkpoint and agree backlog priorities?

Marco Li: +1. can we split by customer-impact vs infra-cost? customers keep asking for per-tenant isolation but that significantly increases capacity overhead.

Priya Sharma: from product POV customers fall into two cohorts: (1) enterprise regulated customers needing hard isolation and audit, (2) ai-native startups who want cheaper, best-effort isolation. recommendation: two-track roadmap.

Eliot Chen: two-track makes sense. engineering question: do we implement strict tenant isolation via node-level slice (reserved capacity) or via routing policy + soft eviction? tradeoffs: node-level gives stronger guarantees but needs provisioning + slower launch.

Ava Dunn: agree. propose we define 3 launch tiers and gating:
- Tier A: Dedicated isolation (node-slice, SLA, KMS) — GA requires capacity planner, billing model, and infra-side autoscaler.
- Tier B: Routing-backed isolation (anti-affinity, soft eviction, quota fencing) — GA requires routing policy DSL, rollout tooling, and perf regression <10% latency delta.
- Tier C: Best-effort affinity (weighting, region preference) — experimental/early access.

Ruth (cs): customers pushing for Tier B right now (want isolation without full Dedicated cost). they’ll accept soft guarantees if we provide observability + escape hatches.

Marco Li: if Tier B is highest near-term priority, we should scope minimal API surface and a small rule language. rough sketch:
```
routing_rule {
  match: tenant_id in [t-123]
  action: prefer_zone("us-east-1a")
  fallback: public_pool
  isolation_level: soft_eviction
}
```
We need to productize fallback semantics.

Priya Sharma: important: customer contracts require documented SLOs for isolation behavior. for Tier B we can promise "attempt strong affinity; may fallback under congestion" and provide metrics to customers (affinity_success_rate, fallbacks).

Eliot Chen: operational concerns: soft eviction means we must implement fast tenant throttles and cross-tenant spill detection. also need canary plan for rollout to avoid cascade eviction. propose a canary that routes 5% traffic of selected tenant groups into new policy and monitors: affinity_success_rate, 95th latency, token cost.

Ava Dunn: good. can we agree on launch criteria checklist for Tier B? my draft:
- routing DSL + UI to create policies
- runtime enforcement with prefix cache safety checks
- telemetry: affinity_success_rate, fallback_count, latencies per-tenant
- fallback semantics documented + SDK/client error responses
- rollback policy + automatic fallback to public_pool if eviction rate > X
- performance target: p95 latency delta < 15% vs baseline

Marco Li: suggest tightening p95 delta to 10% for high-tier customers. maybe use gradated SLOs: 10% for enterprise beta, 15% for general availability.

Ruth (cs): customers will want an SLA variant. we should capture which customers want what so sales can surface.

Priya Sharma: timeline ask — can we do a Tier B pilot in Q4? engineering estimate?

Eliot Chen: rough engineering estimate: 6 wks for rule language + enforcement MVP, 4 wks for telemetry + dashboard, 3 wks for canary infra + safety checks = 13 wks. with parallel work and prioritization maybe 10 wks. so Q4 pilot is tight but achievable if we cut scope (no UI, api-only pilot).

Marco Li: tradeoff decision: cut UI, focus on API + telemetry. also postpone per-tenant billing until Tier A.

Ava Dunn: sounds good. action items:
- Eliot: produce RFC with enforcement design + failure modes (due EOD Friday)
- Marco: prototype routing DSL docs + examples (due next Wed)
- Priya: collect customer priority list and desired SLOs (due next Tue)
- Ruth: flag top 3 customers to engage for pilot (due next Tue)

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: infra-canary-service -> staging at 2024-11-01T03:00Z :rocket:

Ruth (cs): i'll start outreach for pilot interest. note — legal asked about audit logs for Tier B. can we scope minimal audit events?

Eliot Chen: yes, we'll emit policy_decision, fallback_event, and eviction_trigger. that's included in RFC.

Ava Dunn: thanks all. leaving thread open for any objections. if none by EOD Friday we'll lock plan and start tickets. :thumbsup:
